figures.caption: Diamonds show session medians of paired established-DoH minus UDP differences; smaller grey dots show every observed window median. The dashed line is the fixed Nov20 calibration forecast, kept separate from new observations. Shading marks illustrative ±1 and ±2 ms sensitivity bands, not equivalence or utility limits. Missing/running sessions are labeled and contribute no outcome points. Three scheduled sessions occur on one evening, not on independent days.

Each cell categorizes the signed session paired median at a predeclared threshold of 0.5, 1, 2 or 5 ms. L means below −τ, I inside [−τ,+τ], and H above +τ; exact boundaries are inside. The first group is the frozen Nov20 forecast and the other groups are actual completed session statistics. Question marks indicate unavailable sessions. Inside-band medians do not establish equivalence, and these categories are not paired-observation exceedance rates.

Bars are medians of absolute individual paired differences; black dots are absolute values of the signed paired medians. Percentages are the fraction of complete pairs with |Δ| > 2 ms, with denominators reported in the numerical tables. These are different summaries: cancellation in a signed median does not mean individual pair differences are small. The dotted 2 ms reference is an illustrative sensitivity level.

Top: each observed Google treatment marginal median by session/window. Lines only guide the eye; sampling gaps remain. Bottom: marginal window medians centered separately within each session and treatment. Point colors identify sessions. Correlation summaries are reported separately for verified build groups without p-values. Marginal co-movement cannot identify a cache, routing, resolver, CPU or packet-level mechanism; medians of paired differences remain distinct from differences of marginal medians.
